newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh who arrived yesterday from Bangkok will meet President Ramos this morning to get Manila's support for his campaign to regain power in his country. (JOURNAL/MALAYA/TIMES)

- Manila police are set to file multiple homicide charges today against at least eight persons believed responsible for the death of seven tourists from Hong Kong when the sightseeing ferry boat where they were riding in, together with 35 other visitors, capsized in Manila Bay Friday for alleged overloading. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Thirty senior police officials will assume new assignments today as part of what President Ramos said was a continuing reorganisation of the Philippine National Police. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Philippine central bank plans to stay out of the foreign exchange market this week even as the peso is expected to soon breach the 30 to dollar mark, the lowest ever for the embattled currency. (BUSINESSWORLD/TIMES)
- The national government chalked up a budget surplus of 5.7 billion pesos in the first seven months of the year as it tigthened its belt during the period. (TODAY)
- The Philippines has earned another credit upgrade, this time from an Italian export insurance agency. (STAR/CHRONICLE)
